text:
maria-plat: quick flag — noticed spikes in 413s from the embeddings route when clients send mixed-dim arrays. Happened across a couple customers in US-west yesterday. cc @aj @maxw
aj: ugh, good catch. do we have an example payload and the splitter behavior?
maxw: paste from preflight:
```
X-Vec-Dims: [512, 768, 512]
Content-Length: 34MB
route: /v1/embeddings
```
maria-plat: splitter decided to shard into 3 fragments (512/768/512) and attempted to route all to the vector service. two fragments hit a per-shard payload limit and returned 413.
kate-ui: UX ask — console currently only shows "payload failure" logs. can we surface "expected fragments" + per-fragment size so customers understand why their batch failed? :thinking:
aj: yes please. we should show the splitter decision before the request is accepted (preflight). even just an estimate: fragments=3, per_fragment_bytes=~11.3MB, would help.
telemetry-bot: metric emitting: emb.splitter.requests=7, emb.splitter.splits=21, emb.server.413=5, emb.client.dim_mismatch=3
maxw: internal debate — two options: (A) fail early with 400 and rich explanation (recommended for strict contract), (B) auto-split and retry so client gets best-effort result. both have tradeoffs: A offloads cost to client, B increases server-side work and billing complexity.
aj: my vote is A for public API v1: fail early with a helpful message and preflight endpoint to get split plan. we can add an opt-in header for auto-split in v2: `X-Embeddings-AutoSplit: true`.
maria-plat: agree on early fail as default. but for gating enterprise customers we should offer auto-split as a paid policy (and quota implications). need to tie billing and quota dashboards to split_count so we don't surprise customers.
kate-ui: for the console change: new panel on the embeddings request inspector: "Split plan (preflight)" with: predicted_fragments, largest_fragment_bytes, estimated_token_cost, and a CTA: "Enable Auto-split for this key". mockup incoming.
maxw: telemetry: we should tag split outcomes by routing policy that handled it (e.g., preferred_region, fallback_variant). add dims_histogram metric so we can detect common mixed-dim patterns.
telemetry-bot: suggestion added: emit emb.splitter.dim_combo_count, emb.splitter.split_success_rate, emb.splitter.auto_split_optins
aj: operational concern — if we allow auto-split, routers need to be aware of rate quotas per-shard. Otherwise a single incoming mixed batch could blow per-shard TPS and cause cascading backpressure. we need per-fragment quota accounting and a pre-allocate token budget.
maxw: agree. propose policy: allocate budget = ceil(total_tokens / fragments) and decrement per-shard quota atomically. if any shard quota would be exceeded, reject with 429 and include which shard.
maria-plat: can we keep rejection text machine-readable? e.g., {code: "split_quota_exceeded", details: {fragments:3, shard:1, shard_quota:1200}} so SDKs can surface better UX.
kate-ui: SDKs should interpret that and surface inline suggestions: "Try smaller batch" or "Enable Auto-split (enterprise)" with a one-click toggle if allowed.
aj: rollout plan: implement preflight + structured error first (canary 10% on prod traffic). collect metrics for 2 weeks. next, console preflight view, then auto-split opt-in for Enterprise.
infra-bot: deploy queued: service/embeddings-splitter v2 -> canary group 1 (2024-05-16T02:00Z)
maxw: small PR note — we should include `X-Vec-Estimated-Fragments` header in preflight responses for observability and allow proxies to do routing decisions.
maria-plat: one more ask: add a console alert rule template: when emb.server.413 spikes > 3% for 1h, page platform-eng and product. We've been missing these early signals.
telemetry-bot: alert template created: emb.splitter.413_rate > 0.03 for 1h -> notify @platform-eng @prod
aj: thanks all. I'll open two tickets: PRE-553 preflight + structured errors, and OPS-872 per-shard quota accounting spec. tagging @security for any data-flow implications for Enterprise auto-split. :thumbsup:
maxw: I'll follow up with the router change set and a small integration test sim that generates mixed-dim payloads. aim to have a draft by EOD tomorrow. :eyes:
